sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Treaty (1996, as amended)
European Union–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant institution d'un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Grand-Ducal implementing acts transposing EU Directive 2015/849 and EU Directive 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identification card of each ultimate beneficial owner and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the individual's country of residence or an authorized notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or extract from business register of any corporate shareholder evidencing the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent registration authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney authorizing the Luxembourg incorporation agent and manager to act on behalf of the partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Granted by the partners and authenticated by a notary in the country of signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of funds declaration for the initial contribution, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the contributor in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, partners and managers must be screened against the UN Consolidated List, the EU Combined List of restrictive measures, and Luxembourg national financial sanctions lists. PEP screening is mandatory under Luxembourg AML/CFT law and CSSF prudential expectations. OFAC screening is not directly mandated by Luxembourg law but may be required by corresponding cross-border banks and payment processors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal — www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be entered in Latin script. French is the official registry language; non-Latin names must be transliterated into French or German. The statutory suffix 'SCSp' or the full phrase 'Société en commandite spéciale' is mandatory for this entity type.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR rejects a proposed name, the filer may submit a written objection to the RCS registry unit within 10 business days. If the objection is refused, an administrative appeal may be filed before the Tribunal d'arrondissement (Commercial Chamber) within one month of the refusal notification. The applicant may also immediately file an alternate name through the LBR portal. No formal extension of a name reservation exists; a cleared name must be used in the incorporation filing within the 30-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are generally permissible for an SCSp pursuing this non-regulated e-commerce activity, provided that a licensed domiciliation agent maintains a physical Luxembourg registered office and standard correspondence-receiving facilities. Use of a mere post-office box is not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (circa 5% annual probability). No mandatory physical inspection is imposed on an unregulated SCSp; on-site inspection risk increases only if tax-residence challenges or AML red flags arise.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notary fee for authentication of SCSp partnership agreement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) via LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation services, first year
AML/KYC, PEP and sanctions clearance procedures for all UBOs and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider or law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate documents, passports and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and/or consulates of document origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee per document (estimated 50–150 USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and review of the SCSp partnership agreement in French and English
Name clearance request and pre-incorporation reserved-name procedure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg registered agent or law firm

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Part I on partnership forms; SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 11 July 2013, notably Articles 1(7), 24-30 and 908-1 to 908-8; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 December 2013 on RCS filings
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 2, avenue John F. Kennedy, L-1855 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société / Statuts) lodged electronically for RCS registration (déclaration de constitution)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: an SCSp has no statutory minimum capital and no paid-up capital requirement; contributions are freely fixed in the Partnership Agreement; no escrow account is required; capital may be contributed in cash, in kind, or in industry and is recorded in capital accounts
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Partnership Agreement of the SCSp, presented to this meeting, is approved and adopted in full, establishing the registered office at [address], Luxembourg, and the business purpose of retail sales via the internet (ISIC 4791). RESOLVED, that the subscription of partnership interests by the Initial Limited Partner, as reflected in the capital accounts, is accepted in accordance with the Partnership Agreement. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Manager (Gérant) with sole authority to represent the Partnership, open bank accounts, engage legal and tax advisors, and file all statutory returns. RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the General Partner prior to this resolution in furtherance of formation are ratified and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Signing of the Partnership Agreement (Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (for certified form) or General Partner by private writing with authenticated signatures; e-signature via LuxTrust
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Partnership Agreement containing the registered office, business purpose (DTC online retail, ISIC 4791), the fully liable General Partner, the Limited Partners whose liability is capped at their capital commitments, and profit-sharing rules. Execute the instrument before a notary or in private writing. For an SCSp an authentic deed is not mandatory unless real estate is contributed. Keep the signed original for the RCS filing agent.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if executed by a representative
Term sheet on capital commitments and profit sharing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or parties identify defects, execute a rectification deed or addendum before filing; re-signature by all partners; no RCS impact before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic filing counter (eRCS portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A registered filing agent (or Luxembourg counsel) submits the signed Partnership Agreement and the standard RCS filing form electronically, together with identification evidence and proof of registered office. Pay the court registration fee of approximately EUR 30 via the portal. The RCS assigns the registration number and issues the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: RCS standard filing form (formulaire de dépôt)
Passport copies of the General Partner and Limited Partners
Notarized or certified signature specimen of the General Partner
Domiciliation agreement or lease for the registered office
Identity of the filing agent or authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a notice of query (demande de complément), provide the requested clarifications or documents within the given deadline (typically 1 month); if the business purpose is challenged, amend the object clause and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legilux / Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration data to RESA for publication. Verify that the publication notice accurately states the legal form (SCSp), registered office, and identity of the General Partner. No separate user action is required for a standard filing, but counsel should monitor the issuance of the RESA extract and store it as part of the corporate book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains an error, the General Partner must file a request for rectification with the RCS/Legilux, supported by the original documents; republish the corrected notice to maintain legal certainty vis-à-vis third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and VAT Registration (Income Tax Number and Luxembourg VAT Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct tax registration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the opening declaration (déclaration de début d'activité) with the ACD to obtain the income tax number (matricule). Apply for the Luxembourg VAT number with the AEDT. The SCSp is treated as tax-transparent; limited partners are taxed on their share of profits at their level; the corporate General Partner, if any, is subject to corporate income tax on its management fee/general partner share. For cross-border DTC sales to EU consumers, register for the OSS scheme (or IOSS) to settle distance-selling VAT.
required_dossiers: Identity and residence details of all partners
Sales and procurement forecast for VAT positioning (domestic supplies, distance sales, OSS)
Registered office lease or domiciliation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT/ACD queries the application, provide a written explanation of the pass-through allocation and the intended VAT treatment of DTC e-commerce; re-submit through the eCDF or MyGuichet platform; escalate to a Luxembourg tax advisor if a fiscal domiciliation review is triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Registration (Employer and Partner Status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS if staff will be hired for the online operations, and enroll employees within 8 days of their starting work. Register the General Partner with the CCSS as an independent solidary liable worker if he or she actively carries out management activity. Obtain the social security employer number and respect monthly contribution declarations.
required_dossiers: Employment contracts or management mandate of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS issues inconsistencies (e.g., duplicate registrations), file a written rectification request and deregister inactive employers; secure exemption if no employees are engaged by certifying the absence of staff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Activation of E-Commerce Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institutions supervised by the CSSF and payment service providers approved by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a professional bank account in the SCSp's name, providing the RCS registration certificate, the Partnership Agreement, and KYC/AML documentation on the beneficial owner(s). Apply to the chosen payment providers (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe) for a merchant account linked to the Luxembourg VAT number and the legal entity; complete the underwriting review for cross-border card acquiring. The account is necessary for capital contributions and daily DTC sales collection.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration (Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019)
Bank reference letters and business plan of the online store
Pro-forma invoice of the payment provider / Shopify subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC/AML documentation, provide a clear ownership chart, source of funds declaration, and transaction volume projections; if rejected, re-apply with a Tier-2 Luxembourg or EU bank (including PSD2-licensed neobanks) supported by counsel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the activity is a free-access e-commerce service; the Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale de l'industrie) is the licensing authority only for industrial undertakings, which this DTC brand does not operate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or trading operating license is required in Luxembourg for internet retail (ISIC 4791); only the RCS registration and, where applicable, a municipal commercial permit for storage facilities may be needed if a warehouse is opened

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category: no listed installation under the Environmental Impact Assessment Law of 22 May 2008; no EIA, environmental operating permit, or registration is required for a pure online reseller without physical production
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to production; the company must however comply with the Waste Law of 21 March 2017 for packaging, the WEEE Directive for sold electronics (take-back obligations via Ecolog/Valorlux), and the EU Single-Use Plastics Directive reporting if the DTC brand sells packaged goods

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate is required for a dematerialized e-commerce office. The registered office and any ordinary office premises must satisfy the Code du travail (workplace safety, electrical inspections, first-aid equipment) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation on fire prevention in buildings. If a fulfilment/warehouse is added, a municipal occupancy and fire-safety inspection (inspection de la protection civile) will be mandatory before shelving and packing activity starts.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg VAT Department; official e-services via MyGuichet.lu and the AEDT VAT e-file portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SCSp obtains its national business number (matricule) from the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), then applies for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU...) with the AEDT Bureau d'imposition de la TVA. Non-resident EU sellers may register directly for Luxembourg VAT; non-EU sellers must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative unless an exemption or special OSS regime applies. Registration is mandatory before commencing taxable supplies and may be filed by a manager or authorised representative. No minimum capital or statutory licence is required for the SCSp DTC webstore activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box regime. The SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent for income tax purposes; no election to be taxed as a corporation exists. Available limited elections relate to VAT: small-enterprise exemption waiver, Union OSS registration for cross-border B2C e-commerce, and Import One-Stop-Shop for low-value import consignments. Anti-hybrid rules under EU ATAD may impose 'reverse hybrid' entity-level taxation on a transparent SCSp if a non-resident partner treats it as opaque and the mismatch is not otherwise neutralised.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR. A Luxembourg-established online retailer is generally registrable from its first economic activity; the domestic small-enterprise exemption is up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover for Luxembourg-established traders, with an option to register. For intra-EU distance sales to Luxembourg consumers, the harmonised EUR 10,000 EU-wide OSS threshold applies; exceeding it requires VAT accounting and registration in Luxembourg through OSS. No separate local turnover threshold applies to a permanent Luxembourg-establishment DTC brand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no tax-authority digital stamping and no mandatory private-sector e-invoicing API. VAT returns and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically through the AEDT eCDF/e-file channel; OSS returns are filed through the Luxembourg OSS portal. Invoices must meet EU VAT invoice requirements. Mandatory e-invoicing (Peppol BIS/EN 16931) applies only to Luxembourg public procurement and does not apply to Shopify/PayPal/Stripe B2C payments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Luxembourg VAT applies to (i) exports of goods to non-EU destinations if the supplier possesses documentary proof of exit from the EU; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to taxable consumers in other EU member states where the customer communicates a valid EU VAT ID and the goods are dispatched to that member state; and (iii) certain ancillary services directly related to export transactions. For a global DTC webstore selling from Luxembourg to non-EU customers, the sale is eligible for 0% VAT if the goods leave the EU. B2C digital services and intra-EU cross-border B2C distance sales follow destination taxation and cannot be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (EAD/SAD) in the exporting member state, with itemised CN codes, weights and values
Transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU: Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or air waybill
Commercial invoice/order confirmation matching the SCSp seller and DTC customer
Proof of payment for the transaction and, where applicable, the inward foreign-currency remittance certificate/inward remittance advice from the receiving bank
Customs proof-of-export record (electronic or stamped exit confirmation) and, when applicable, delivery confirmation from an independent logistics provider
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may conduct a VAT audit and reassess zero-rated exports within the standard five-year assessment period, extended to ten years in cases of fraud. Failure to substantiate export or intra-Community supply triggers immediate recomputation of Luxembourg VAT at the applicable rate (17% standard or appropriate reduced rate), plus late interest of 0.8% per month. Fraudulent zero-rating claims can lead to administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 (or up to twice the evaded tax), criminal sanctions including imprisonment, and personal liability of SCSp managers for VAT debts where bad faith or abusive manoeuvre is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) / Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member and applies full capital and current account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital. No general foreign exchange controls exist for non-resident investors. Profit remittances, dividends, and distributions from an SCSp are freely transferable without prior authorization, subject to standard AML/KYC reporting thresholds and tax reporting obligations. Withholding tax treatment may apply to certain outbound payments, but remittance itself is unrestricted. The euro is fully convertible, and cross-border payment operations are governed by EU Payment Services Directive and SEPA/ SWIFT rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation or holding period applies to export receipts in Luxembourg. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency, credited to resident or non-resident accounts, and freely used for trade settlements, intercompany funding, or FX hedging. Reporting obligations arise only under balance-of-payments statistics regulations, requiring nominal filing of cross-border transactions above thresholds to the BCL via registered credit institutions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse de l'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately feasible; Luxembourg recognizes licensed Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions under CSSF supervision. Cross-border digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, MultiPass) can provide ancillary euro IBANs and FX services, but they generally require an underlying local credit institution account for settlement. For an SCSp, EMI accounts cannot serve as the exclusive treasury vehicle due to corporate banking expectations, capital commitment tracking, and investor-side verification. Legal constraints include EMI sandbox limits, transaction monitoring, and inability to hold client assets as an escrow agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and ultimate beneficial owners is generally mandated for non-resident SCSp structures in Luxembourg. Most tier-1 banks require at least one in-person meeting in Luxembourg or with a notarized apostilled identification process; remote video onboarding is possible only for low-risk, single-country structures. Non-resident partners or foreign general partners may alternatively authorize a Luxembourg-based fiduciary or professional partner to attend the meeting if the constitutive documents expressly permit representation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident opaque SCSp with a foreign general partner and silent limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement, up-to-date extract from Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), registered office agreement, UBO register filing confirmation (RBE), and a full partner disclosure chart with passport copies and source of wealth documentation for all 25%+ owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce DTC brand relying on multiple payment service providers without a existing corporate banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft commercial contracts and terms of service from Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe, platform settlement statements for the last six months, business plan, projected transaction flows, and an explanation of the payment split mechanism including refund and chargeback handling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border disbursements to first-time suppliers in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier due diligence file including business registration certificate, trade licence, bank confirmation letter, passport copies of supplier directors, invoices and purchase orders, and a written explanation of the supply chain rationale and customs/import documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from assets accumulated in a foreign jurisdiction with no clear paper trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the source account, tax returns or wealth declarations, sale agreement if funds originated from a business exit, inheritance or gift deed, and a signed declaration of any liechtenstein or offshore entities involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp tax classification ambiguity triggering a bank's FATCA/CRS classification review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Luxembourg law firm confirming the SCSp is tax-transparent unless opted into corporation tax, a completed CRS self-certification form (CRS-C), a valid taxpayer identification number for each partner, and partnership agreements clarifying profit-sharing ratios.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident partners should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the partner's bank to the SCSp's operational euro account in Luxembourg. The payment reference must include the purpose code S301 (direct investment in shares/equity) under the ECB's Balance of Payments harmonized categorization, or FINREP taxonomy equivalent. The bank must receive a board/GP resolution authorizing the capital call, a countersigned capital contribution deed, and the shareholding/partnership percentage schedule. Each inbound wire should be accompanied by a KYC-relevant beneficiary legal entity identifier (LEI of the SCSp) and a clear economic purpose statement. For large contributions exceeding €1,000,000, the SCSp should prepare an anti-money laundering statement covering source of wealth and the underlying sale transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to international suppliers should use the SWIFT MT103 standard clearing instruction via Luxembourg's TARGET2/SCT infrastructure. For high-value shipments or recurring inventory purchases, suppliers may require a Documentary Letter of Credit, executed through a Luxembourg commercial bank. Domestic and EU supplier payments can be effected via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) using BIC/IBAN with no FX exposure. Non-Euro purchases require a spot FX transaction with the banking partner before issuing the MT103. The bank will apply a purpose code based on the nature of the payment, e.g., S101 (merchandise export/import), and will request supporting invoices or a customs declaration for trade compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (plain vanilla deliverable forward against EUR)
NDF (Non-Deliverable Forward) for restricted/less-liquid currency pairs not deliverable with a Luxembourg bank
Cross-currency swap (fixed-to-fixed or floating-to-fixed) to hedge balance-sheet exposures
FX Options (European-style put/call) for asymmetric hedging strategy
Currency futures listed on EU-regulated venues if margin efficient

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE déclaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 31 March following each calendar year; within one month of any change in ultimate beneficial owners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 under the amended Law of 13 January 2019; criminal penalties and imprisonment for directors/general partners in case of willful omission; daily penalty for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filing with regular RCS record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of financial year-end for the SCSp, after approval by partners; extensions available under specific circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 1,000 under commercial law; forced filing injunctions by the commercial court; persistent failure may lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur les revenus)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Income Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For financial year ending 31 December, due 31 May of the following year; electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu due 31 December of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 0.6% per month on assessed liability; administrative fines up to EUR 20,000 for persistent failure; criminal sanctions for fraudulent misdeclaration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is compulsory if the SCSp exceeds two of three criteria on a consolidated basis: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.4 million, average headcount 50. A small or micro SCSp (partner-managed, wholly owned by individuals for their own account) is generally exempt; fund vehicle audits may be required under CSSF regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Luxembourg, PCL) as derived from the EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS permitted for certain regulated financial entities or when the partnership is listed; consolidated accounts under IFRS/Lux GAAP if group thresholds are met.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an up-to-date register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) at the registered office. The general partner shall file an annual confirmation with the RBE at least once every calendar year or within one month of any change in ownership. Any transfer of partnership interests must be recorded in the register of partners and separately reported to the RBE. Failure to update after a shareholding transfer, even if non-material, triggers immediate penalty exposure.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,500 - 3,500 USD (typical corporate-service-provider annual fee for Luxembourg SCSp registered office, resident agent and compliance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 USD for small SCSp not crossing audit thresholds; 12,000 - 25,000 USD if a statutory audit becomes compulsory due to undertaking size or investor requirement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17.0% CIT headline; plus 7% solidarity surcharge and communal business tax (Luxembourg City 6.75%), aggregate top rate ±24.94% for a taxable corporate partner
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. IP box: 80% exemption of qualifying IP income (effective ±4.99% aggregate). Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income (≥10% holding, 12-month holding). SCSp pass-through: no entity-level CIT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax / impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and integrated communal business tax computation — mandatory e-filing via MyGuichet.lu professional space (eCDF XML schema)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Default: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; accelerated deadlines for advisor-represented filers (FY2024: 30 Sep 2025; FY2025: 31 Jul 2026; FY2026: 31 May 2027; FY2027+: 31 Mar of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, registration number (LBR/RCS), AEDT tax number, VAT number, RBE declaration status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SCSp's Luxembourg tax number and details of the general partner; non-resident limited partners must not be identified as the taxpayer at entity level; attach a partner schedule for profit allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year profit before tax per audited/internally prepared accounts of the commercial activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Shopify/PayPal/Stripe settlement reports to the cash ledger; file supporting payment-rail reconciliations for the online store.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, interest limitation recalculations (ATAD thin-cap), CFC adjustments, excessive royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document arm's-length fees paid to affiliated IP or service entities, especially from a non-resident-owned DTC brand structure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year tax losses against current taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply unlimited carryforward for CIT but five-year limitation for communal business tax; maintain a loss register per partner allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of the share of Luxembourg-source business income for each partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxed in Luxembourg to the extent the SCSp carries on a Luxembourg commercial business; attach a partner allocation statement and respective TRCs where treaty relief is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: ex officio assessment (taxation d'office), automatic 10% surcharge on assessed tax (droit en sus), late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (0.5% as from 1 Jan 2025); administrative fine up to €25,000; criminal liability in case of fraudulent intent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 400 + EU OSS return (VAT) — Luxembourg VAT return and One-Stop-Shop periodic return for B2C distance sales, filed via MyGuichet.lu/OSS portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: VAT return: by the 15th day of the month following the period (monthly/quarterly cycle); OSS return: by the end of the month following the quarter; payment due on same date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Distance sales to EU consumers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT on B2C webstore sales into EU member states
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare via OSS in Luxembourg if distance sales remain below the €10,000 EU cross-border threshold; otherwise register OSS in Luxembourg as the identification member state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Intra-Community/import supplies and Marketplace treatment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Goods imported for fulfilment; treatment of Shopify Payments as payment-acquisition rather than deemed supply
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain proof of customs entry and the underlying electronic-commerce contract to avoid deemed-supplier reclassification by member states.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible input VAT on app fees, logistics, Shopify subscription, advertising
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners should not recover VAT separately; input VAT is recovered centrally by the SCSp/general partner in Luxembourg practice.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing/under-declaration: 10-20% surcharge, late interest, ex officio VAT assessment; penalty of €250-€1,250,000 in AML? No—VAT: fines up to €2,500 per declaration plus 10% adjustment surcharge and criminal sanctions for deliberate omission.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic WHT on dividends distributed by Luxembourg resident commercial companies; SCSp profit distributions to partners are not mechanically subject to dividend WHT because the SCSp is tax-transparent and lacks corporate personality
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief or exemption: (i) obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the partner's residence state; (ii) file the beneficial-ownership and 12-month holding declaration with the AEDT before/at payment; (iii) where WHT was retained, claim refund through the AEDT within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years), with full economic-substance evidence to meet MLI PPT and Luxembourg GAAR.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory WHT on ordinary interest and on royalties in Luxembourg (no source tax on IP royalties or cash-deposit/bank interest); only profit-linked bond interest (intérêts participatifs) suffers 15% WHT; no DTA reduction needed for the 0% category cases.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR: Local File mandatory where net turnover ≥ EUR 50,000,000 OR balance sheet total ≥ EUR 4,000,000 OR gross financial income ≥ EUR 1,000,000 (Art. 56bis LIR); Master File mandatory where consolidated group turnover ≥ EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies no UAE-style statutory ESR; substance is enforced through Art. 6 Steueranpassungsgesetz GAAR, MLI principal-purpose test, ATAD interest/CFC rules and the EU Unshell directive (adopted 2025). The SCSp must demonstrate: Luxembourg registered office, local general partner and decision-making, local bank account, segregated Shopify/PayPal/Stripe settlement reporting, and qualified administrative support.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of DTC webstore revenue, false partner allocation on Form 500, undisclosed Shopify/PayPal/Stripe receivables, fabricated e-commerce losses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio re-assessment plus 10% surcharge, monthly late interest (0.5-0.6%), administrative fine up to €25,000; criminal tax fraud penalties (art. 439 LIR): imprisonment and fine up to €100,000, plus restitution of evaded tax with penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and the general partner can be jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency and penalties where the evasion is attributable to their deliberate acts; criminal prosecution of directors, travel/asset-restraint measures and potential imprisonment up to 5 years in aggravated fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp operating as a letterbox: no Luxembourg office, no local books contracted bookkeeping? no bank account, all management and payments executed abroad for the DTC webstore, treaty-shopping via unsubstantiated TRCs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization (art. 6 Steueranpassungsgesetz), denial of treaty benefits under MLI PPT, retroactive assessment of Luxembourg-source income, 10% penalty surcharge and late interest; EU Unshell directive consequences after transposition: deemed shell result and tax liability transfer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers tolerating the letterbox structure face civil restitution claims, disqualification orders and, in tax-fraud constellations, personal criminal liability; the Luxembourg AEDT may seek payment of corporate tax debts from the general partner of the transparent partnership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No RBE declaration of the beneficial owners of the SCSp; absence of KYC/CDD on limited partners and payment-rail account signatories; failure to maintain AML policy for Shopify_Payments, PayPal and Stripe flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1,250,000 under the Luxembourg AML framework (law of 12 Nov 2004, CRF/compétent authority), fines of €125 to €125,000 and up to 1 year imprisonment for RBE non-compliance; freezing of bank accounts by EPP? no—freezing orders by the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil and criminal liability of the general partner and directors: fines, imprisonment (up to 5 years), professional prohibition for regulated positions, and piercing of limited liability where the partnership veil was used to conceal ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation and arm's length breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing Local/Master File despite thresholds being met; non-arm's-length royalty or SaaS fee to offshore affiliate; artificial profit shift out of the Luxembourg DTC activity; TP doc submitted in English without Luxembourg statutory translation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment of taxable income with 10% surcharge and late interest; fixed penalty up to €1,000 for failure to maintain TP documentation under art. 56bis LIR; disallowance of deductions and potential double taxation without corresponding treaty adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner signing Form 500 is personally liable for the accuracy of TP documentation declarations; deliberate manipulation attracts criminal fraud sanctions and civil restitution claims from the partnership or co-partners.
